title: Before You Touch a Chart
hook: Clear the challenge, pass the Knowledge Check, and save your Check-In to unlock Section 3.

challenge.title: Ready Before You Trade
challenge.subtitle: Real situations. Pick what a prepared trader would do.

rounds.heading: Clean workspace
rounds.prompt: Your chart has 14 indicators, 9 drawings and 3 timeframes stacked on it.
rounds.question: What’s the first fix?

options.label: Add one more indicator to confirm the others
options.feedback: More tools make price harder to read, not easier.

options.label: Strip it back to a few tools you use clearly
options.feedback: Right. A few tools used clearly beats a messy chart.

options.label: Switch timeframes until it looks cleaner
options.feedback: Switching timeframes changes your view, not the clutter.

rounds.heading: Which account?
rounds.prompt: A trader wants to prove they’re consistent before risking any real money.
rounds.question: Which account actually answers that?

options.label: A broker account
options.feedback: A broker account risks your own capital from trade one.

options.label: A simulated account
options.feedback: Right. A simulated account proves consistency with zero financial risk.

options.label: Whichever has the biggest balance
options.feedback: Balance size doesn’t answer the consistency question.

rounds.heading: Pick the order
rounds.prompt: You only want in if price proves it can trade above a level. Until then, you want nothing to happen.
rounds.question: Which order fits?

options.label: Market order
options.feedback: A market order fills right now, at whatever price is available.

options.label: Limit order
options.feedback: A limit order waits for a better price. It doesn’t wait for price to prove a level.

options.label: Stop order
options.feedback: Right. A stop order sits inactive until price reaches the level, then acts like a market order.

rounds.heading: Will it fill?
rounds.prompt: You place a buy limit order at 19,950. Price drops to 19,960, then rallies away.
rounds.question: Did your order fill?

options.label: Yes, it was close enough
options.feedback: A limit only fills at your price or better. Close doesn’t count.

options.label: No, price never reached your limit price
options.feedback: Right. That’s the trade-off: price control, but no guaranteed fill.

rounds.heading: Place the stop
rounds.prompt: You’re long in an uptrend. The higher low that your idea depends on is 18 points below your entry.
rounds.question: Where does the stop belong?

options.label: A comfortable 8 points away, so the loss feels small
options.feedback: Comfort isn’t a reason. A stop belongs where the setup is proven wrong.

options.label: Beyond the higher low that would prove the idea wrong
options.feedback: Right. Your stop protects the plan, not your feelings in the moment.

options.label: No stop, you’ll watch it closely
options.feedback: Watching isn’t a plan. Exits come before entries.

rounds.heading: Size it
rounds.prompt: Same setup, two traders. One uses 1 contract, the other uses 10 after a losing streak to “make it back.”
rounds.question: What’s the real difference?

options.label: Nothing, it’s the same setup
options.feedback: Same setup, very different dollar risk and emotional weight.

options.label: One is sized from a plan, the other from emotion
options.feedback: Right. Size your position, not your ego.

options.label: The 10-contract trade is better because it can win more
options.feedback: It can lose 10 times more too. Sizing comes from the risk plan.

rounds.heading: Read the clock
rounds.prompt: Price breaks a level overnight on thin volume. The same-looking break happens again at the New York open on heavy volume.
rounds.question: Do they carry the same weight?

options.label: Yes, a break is a break
options.feedback: Session context matters. Volume tells you who showed up.

options.label: No, the heavy-volume break carries more real information
options.feedback: Right. A level in London and a level at the New York open don’t carry the same weight.

rounds.heading: Exit plan
rounds.question: What should already be decided? Select everything that applies.

items.label: Whether to move your stop if it gets close

rounds.successFeedback: Exactly. Exits before entries, size from the plan, and no moving the stop out of fear.

questionBank.question: What does switching your chart’s timeframe change?
options: Your view of the same price
questionBank.why: Switching timeframes changes your view, not the market.

questionBank.question: Does adding more drawing tools make a chart easier to read?
options: Yes, more information is always better
No, a cluttered chart makes price harder to read
questionBank.why: A few tools used clearly beats a messy chart.

questionBank.question: What does a prop firm evaluation test?
options: How fast you can grow a balance
Rule-discipline before granting access to capital
Nothing, it’s the same as a broker account
questionBank.why: A prop evaluation tests whether you follow the rules before you get capital access.

questionBank.question: Which account risks your own capital from the very first trade?
questionBank.why: A broker account uses your own money from trade one.

questionBank.question: What’s the trade-off of a market order?
questionBank.why: A market order fills fast, but you don’t control the exact price.

questionBank.question: If price never reaches your limit price, what happens?
options: It fills anyway at the closest price
It turns into a stop order
questionBank.why: A limit only fills at your price or better.

questionBank.question: How does a stop order behave?
options: It sits inactive until price reaches the level, then acts like a market order
It only fills at a better price
questionBank.why: A stop waits for price to prove the level, then executes like a market order.

questionBank.question: Where does a stop loss belong?
options: Where the setup is actually proven wrong
questionBank.why: A stop belongs at the point that proves the idea wrong.

questionBank.question: Price moves toward your stop. You feel nervous and want to move it further away. What does that do?
options: Defeats the reason the stop exists
questionBank.why: Moving your stop out of fear defeats the reason it exists.

questionBank.question: When should a take profit be decided?
options: In advance, as part of the plan
In the moment, based on how you feel
Only after the trade is in profit
questionBank.why: A take profit is planned in advance, not decided in the moment.

questionBank.question: Where should your position size come from?
questionBank.why: Sizing comes from your risk plan, never from mood or a streak.

questionBank.question: Can the same setup be reasonable at one size and reckless at another?
options: No, a good setup is good at any size
Yes, size decides the dollar risk and emotional weight
questionBank.why: Same setup, different size, very different trade.

questionBank.question: Which statement about Asia, London and New York is most accurate?
options: They each behave differently, none is “better,” just different
questionBank.why: Each session has its own character. Know which one you’re in.

questionBank.question: Why does volume matter when you read a move?
options: A move on heavy volume carries more real information than the same move on thin volume
Thin volume moves are always fake
questionBank.why: Volume tells you who showed up for the move.
